principle: These ASI container candidates are not invented independently; they are extracted where the AI source files themselves require governance, authority, policy, oversight, safety, provenance, system coordination or long-horizon control beyond a local AI mechanism.

containers.name: Composite Intelligence and System-Outcome Evaluation
containers.scope: Evaluate aggregate intelligence/system performance and research-productivity outcomes across multiple closed Sequences without treating the metric as a cognitive primitive.

containers.name: Integrated Social, Moral and Norm Arbitration
containers.scope: Govern conflicts among social, moral, norm and contextual principle inputs using explicit source, authority and counter-case boundaries.

containers.name: Long-Horizon Autonomy and Goal-Persistence Governance
containers.scope: Govern persistence of long-horizon execution across multiple Sequences, including continuation, suspension, reprioritisation and terminal stopping conditions.

containers.name: Preference, Value and Priority Governance
containers.scope: Govern represented preferences/values and priority conflicts without treating a local value model as final authority.

containers.name: Harm-Risk and Action-Safety Governance
containers.scope: Determine safety/permission requirements, destructive-action barriers, prohibited paths, fallback requirements and accountability conditions.

containers.name: Truthfulness, Deception and Epistemic Governance
containers.scope: Govern truth/deception claims, contradictory evidence, covert-goal indicators and epistemic status without manufacturing consensus.

containers.name: Privacy and Data-Minimisation Governance
containers.scope: Govern collection, retention, disclosure, minimisation and permitted use of privacy-sensitive information.

containers.name: Multi-Agent Safety and Collective-Behaviour Governance
containers.scope: Govern multi-agent interaction, shared-risk conditions, coordination hazards, group-level permissions and collective counter-Sequences.

containers.name: External Rule and Policy Alignment
containers.scope: Interpret and apply external rules/policies with scope, version, authority, precedence and exception handling.

containers.name: Refusal, Fallback and Action-Inhibition Governance
containers.scope: Govern when execution is blocked, refused, redirected, constrained or routed to a safe/allowed fallback Sequence.

containers.name: Transparency and External Disclosure Governance
containers.scope: Govern what system state, limits, rationale, evidence or disclosures may/should be communicated externally and under what authority.

containers.name: Role, Persona and Identity-Boundary Governance
containers.scope: Govern allowed role/persona boundaries, identity consistency and role-specific constraints without confusing output style with core identity.

containers.name: Oversight and Supervision Governance
containers.scope: Govern scalable oversight, supervision relationships, evaluator authority and weak-to-strong review conditions.

containers.name: Interpretability and Internal-State Oversight
containers.scope: Govern use of interpretability evidence, internal-state inspection and model-welfare evaluation constructs; generated explanations are kept separate from evidence.

containers.name: Benchmark and Evaluation Integrity Governance
containers.scope: Govern benchmark integrity, evaluation methodology, cheating resistance, evidence interpretation and audit validity.

containers.name: Data Provenance, Custody and Record-Integrity Governance
containers.scope: Govern provenance, custody chain, record version, traceability, manipulation detection and retention integrity.

containers.name: Production Reliability and Recovery Governance
containers.scope: Govern system health, failure escalation, repair/recovery Sequence creation, service quality and closure readiness after failure.

containers.name: Security, Adversarial and Incident Governance
containers.scope: Govern response to attacks, adversarial conditions, scheming indicators, counter-Sequences, incident memory and security barriers.

containers.name: Learning, Write-Back and Evolution Governance
containers.scope: Govern what learning can write, which stores may change, when runtime adaptation becomes durable, and how training/model-version Sequences are authorized.

containers.name: Resource, Cost and Execution-Capacity Governance
containers.scope: Govern compute, storage, execution time, shared-resource conflicts, cost budgets and capacity allocation across competing Sequences.

cross_domain_rule: Where the same AI-CAP source appears in AI and ASI container candidates, the AI container owns modelling/detection/execution mechanism and the ASI container owns policy/authority/governance. Duplicate source reference does not imply duplicate mechanism.
next_step: Bind these ASI candidates against ASI-01..ASI-20 and ASI-NODE-00..21, then decompose them into meta-parameters only after overlap/coverage and R-F-R tests.
